findings.title: Crash when location is Google Meet and destinationCalendar is empty
findings.body: In `EventManager.create()` the new code does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and then immediately reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` in `if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar")`. When the event has no destination calendar (e.g. organizer and event type both have none, which `handleNewBooking` now represents as `null`), `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` and accessing `.integration` throws a TypeError, failing the whole booking. The previous code used optional chaining (`evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`) and safely fell back to Cal Video in exactly this scenario — this is the very fallback the comment describes ('Google Meet selected w/o a Google Cal'). Needs `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

findings.title: Non-Google calendar services always use the first destination calendar, so other hosts never get events
findings.body: The PR makes EventManager create one event per host destination calendar by calling `createEvent` with each host's own credential, but the Office365, Lark and CalDAV services still only read the FIRST element of `event.destinationCalendar` (e.g. here `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];` then `\`/me/calendars/${mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId}/events\``). The first element is the organizer's calendar, whose externalId belongs to a different account than the team-member credential being used. For Office365 this posts to a calendar id that doesn't exist in the team member's account (API error, success=false); Lark (lines 128, 164, 192, 237) has the same problem; the CalDAV base service (`packages/lib/CalendarService.ts` line 156) filters its calendar list by the first destination's externalId, matches nothing, and silently returns success without creating any event. Only Google Calendar was updated to pick the destination matching `credentialId`. As a result the stated goal of this PR — every host with any calendar app receiving the event — only works for Google Calendar; Office365/Lark/CalDAV hosts get nothing.

findings.title: Reschedule only deletes the first old calendar event, leaving stale events on other hosts' calendars
findings.body: In `updateAllCalendarEvents`, when `newBookingId` is set (reschedule), the cleanup of the old booking's calendar events uses `booking.references.find((reference) => reference.type.includes("_calendar"))` — a single reference. Now that this PR creates one `_calendar` reference per collective-event host, the old booking can have several calendar references, and only the first host's old event is deleted; the other hosts keep the stale pre-reschedule event on their calendars. This should iterate over all old calendar references (filter) and delete each with its own credentialId/externalCalendarId.

findings.title: Unrelated change inverts organization slug logic for team billing
findings.body: This PR flips `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` while keeping `requestedSlug` also set when billing is enabled. Previously, when team billing was enabled the org slug was deliberately NOT set at creation time (only `requestedSlug`, presumably until billing completed); now the slug is claimed immediately in the billing-enabled flow and never set in the billing-disabled flow. This is unrelated to the destinationCalendar change and inverts the intended behavior of the billing gate.

findings.title: Cancelling all remaining recurring bookings only deletes the first calendar reference per booking
findings.body: The recurring-cancel branch inside the new per-reference loop still does `const bookingRef = updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"))` and deletes only that one event, and it iterates only `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` (the organizer's). With multiple hosts, each updated booking now has several `_calendar` references (one per host credential), so the other hosts' recurring instances are never deleted. Additionally, because this whole block is now nested inside `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`, the entire delete-across-all-credentials routine runs once per reference, issuing duplicate delete calls for the same events.

findings.title: Confirming a collective booking still builds evt with a single destination calendar
findings.body: For bookings requiring confirmation, calendar events are created at confirmation time via `handleConfirmation`/`EventManager.create(evt)`, but the `evt` built here sets `destinationCalendar` to only `[booking.destinationCalendar]` or `[user.destinationCalendar]` — the organizer's single calendar. The per-host destination calendars of the other collective hosts are never added, so confirming a collective opt-in booking still only creates the event on the organizer's calendar — the exact bug this PR sets out to fix remains in the confirmation path. The same gap exists in the payment-success flows (`packages/features/ee/payments/api/webhook.ts` and `paypal-webhook.ts`), which also build `evt` with only the booking/organizer destination calendar before calling `eventManager.create(evt)`.

findings.title: updateLocation creates new references without externalCalendarId/credentialId
findings.body: In `updateLocation`, `referencesToCreate` now uses `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId`, but these results come from `updateAllCalendarEvents` → `CalendarManager.updateEvent`, whose returned `EventResult` never sets `externalId` or `credentialId`. Previously these were populated from `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId`/`?.credentialId`. `editLocation.handler` then persists these references (`references: { create: updatedResult.referencesToCreate }`), so after a location edit the new references lack the credential/calendar ids that later update/delete flows depend on.

findings.title: Reschedule-request deletes calendar events with the organizer's credential instead of each reference's credential
findings.body: Calendar cleanup here builds `credentialsMap` from the requesting user's credentials keyed by type, then for every booking reference calls `getCalendar(credentialsMap.get(bookingRef.type))` and deletes `bookingRef.uid`. With this PR, collective bookings have references pointing at OTHER hosts' credentials/calendars; deleting those events with the organizer's credential of the same app type will not find the event (different account), so the other hosts' calendar events survive a reschedule request. The per-reference `credentialId` (now stored thanks to this PR) should be used to load the correct credential, as done in `handleCancelBooking`.

findings.title: updateEvent fallback find compares against a known-falsy externalCalendarId
findings.body: `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` — in the fallback branch `externalCalendarId` is falsy by definition, so the `find` predicate compares each calendar's externalId against null/undefined/'' and effectively never matches, yielding `calendarId: undefined` for the update call. The old code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. Bookings whose reference lacks `externalCalendarId` (legacy rows) will now attempt to update `calendars/undefined/events/...` and fail, whereas before they updated the destination calendar. The same dead predicate exists in `deleteEvent` (line ~317), where it silently degrades to deleting from "primary" instead of the destination calendar.

findings.title: Hangout-link patch uses possibly-undefined calendarId after primary fallback
findings.body: In `createEvent`, the insert uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` that writes the hangout link into the description uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar` directly. When no destination calendar matches the credential (the "primary" fallback path), `selectedCalendar` is `undefined`, so the patch targets `calendars/undefined/...` and the event description never gets the Meet link. Previously `selectedCalendar` was always at least "primary".

findings.title: loadUsers refactor drops organization.slug from dynamic booking user query
findings.body: The rewritten `loadUsers` for the dynamic (no eventTypeId) path selects `...userSelect.select, credentials: true, metadata: true` but no longer selects `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` that the old query included. Any downstream code reading `user.organization?.slug` for dynamic collective bookings (org context/branding/URLs) will now get `undefined`. This change is also unrelated to the destinationCalendar fix.

findings.title: destinationCalendar falls back to null here but [] everywhere else, and team calendars are silently dropped when null
findings.body: The new evt initializer uses `: null` when neither eventType nor organizer has a destination calendar, while every other call site in this PR (confirm, cancel, payment webhooks, bookingReminder, etc.) uses `[]`. This makes the webhook payload shape inconsistent (BOOKING_CREATED/BOOKING_REQUESTED send `destinationCalendar: null`, BOOKING_REJECTED sends `[]`), which consumers must special-case — the e2e expectations updated in this PR encode exactly that inconsistency. Additionally, the subsequent `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op when the value is null, so for a collective event whose organizer has no destination calendar, the other hosts' calendars are silently discarded.
